extracted.intended_audience: applicants and agents preparing PCT international patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing the formal parts of a PCT international application (claims, drawings, abstract and other formal requirements) to meet PCT Rules and Articles during international and national phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must commence on a new sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must commence on a new sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As outlined in paragraph 5.105; ensure claims begin on a separate sheet distinct from the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims may include tables if desirable in view of the subject matter involved (Rule 11.10(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables must be included in the text of the relevant claim; they may not be annexed to the claims nor may reference be made to tables contained in the description (refer to paragraph 5.109).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious mistakes in the claims can be rectified following the procedure under Rule 91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure explained in paragraphs 11.033–11.044. Omission of an entire sheet of the claims cannot be rectified without affecting the international filing date (see paragraphs 6.025–6.026). Recommended to request rectification only if mistake is liable to affect the international search; otherwise rectify by amending the claims (refer to paragraph 5.127).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be amended during the international phase under specified Articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may be amended under Article 19 on receipt of the international search report (see paragraphs 9.004–9.011); they may also be amended during international preliminary examination if a demand is filed (see paragraphs 10.024 and 10.067) and during the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: When drawings are required
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be included when necessary for the understanding of the invention (Article 3(2), Article 7, Rule 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if not strictly necessary, applicant may include drawings if the nature of the invention admits illustration by drawings. Any designated Office may require drawings to be filed during the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspectives, exploded views, sections, cross-sections, details on a different scale, flow sheets, diagrams and graphic parameter representations are considered drawings (Rule 7.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings include technical diagrams and graphic representations that express relationships between parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulae and tables not drawings (unless submitted as drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae and tables are not considered drawings, but may be submitted as drawings (Rule 11.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted as drawings they become subject to the same requirements as drawings (see paragraphs 5.131–5.133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must be on separate sheets and not include description/claims/abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be presented on one or more separate sheets and may not be included in the description, claims or the abstract (Rules 11.10, 11.11, 11.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings may not contain text matter except a single word or words when absolutely indispensable. Any drawing meeting the Rule 11 requirements must be accepted in the national phase. A file reference may be indicated on each sheet of the drawings (refer to paragraph 5.105).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must allow direct reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be presented so as to admit of direct reproduction by photography, electrostatic processes, photo offset and microfilming (Rule 11.2(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure line quality, contrast and paper quality support reproduction in multiple copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical paper requirements for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on A4 paper (29.7 x 21.0 cm), flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny and durable (Rule 11.2(a), 11.2(b), 11.2(c), 11.3, 11.5, 11.6(c), 11.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets must be free from creases/cracks/folds, reasonably free from erasures, free from alterations/overwriting/interlineations. Only one side may be used. Usable surface must not exceed 26.2 x 17.0 cm. No frames around usable surface. Minimum margins: top and left 2.5 cm; right 1.5 cm; bottom 1.0 cm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of figures on sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures constituting the drawings must be grouped together on a sheet or sheets without waste of space, but clearly separated from each other (Rule 11.10(d), 11.13(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures should not be separated by lines. Place figures compactly but distinctly separated so they are easy to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation of figures on sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be set out upright as far as possible; if not, they may be placed sideways with tops on left-hand side (Rule 11.10(d), 11.13(j)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a figure is broader than high, it may be rotated; if multiple figures on same sheet, they should share the same orientation. Applies similarly to tables and chemical/mathematical formulae.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and type of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings should contain as many figures as necessary to adequately show the claimed invention; views may be plan, elevation, section, perspective, detail or exploded views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One figure should not be placed upon or within the outline of another. Use the simplest set of views compatible with fully and unambiguously defining the object (see paragraphs 5.136–5.138).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a general figure for improvements to existing devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where invention concerns improvements to an existing device, a general figure is desirable to indicate where the improvement is situated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a general figure (often first) showing the improved device; avoid unnecessary depiction of entire larger systems if irrelevant (e.g., whole automobile for a pump improvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize number of views; choose simplest representative views
rubrics_metrics.description: It is sufficient to choose views which are most representative and contain the minimum of hidden parts so the object is completely and unambiguously defined by the smallest possible number of views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes a single perspective view may replace multiple views. Choose the simplest view compatible with clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial figures across sheets must assemble unambiguously
rubrics_metrics.description: Where figures on two or more sheets form a single complete figure, they must be arranged so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing any part (Rule 11.13(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial figures must be linkable edge to edge; no partial figure may contain parts of another partial figure. For very long figures divided across sheets, include a smaller scale figure showing the whole and positions of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet numbering of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: All sheets of drawings must be numbered in the center of either the top or bottom of each sheet but not in the margin (Rule 11.7, Section 207(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numbers larger than reference signs and a separate numbering series for drawings. Format: sheet_number/total_sheets (e.g., 2/5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and use of 'Fig.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Different figures must be numbered in Arabic numerals consecutively and independently of sheet numbering; numbers should be preceded by 'Fig.' in whatever language (Rule 11.13(k), Rule 49.5(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single figure suffices, it should not be numbered nor should 'Fig.' appear. Numbers/letters must be simple and clear. Partial figures forming one complete figure may use the same number with a capital letter suffix (e.g., Fig. 7B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement order of figures on a sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should preferably be set out in ascending numerical order from left to right and top to bottom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one figure is a larger-scale detail of another, number each separately and consecutively where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution of drawings: line quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be executed in durable, black, uniformly thick and well-defined lines and strokes (Rule 11.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line thickness must account for scale, nature and legibility. Drafting instruments should ordinarily be used except where nature of figure precludes (e.g., irregular diagrams or ornamental structures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of different line thicknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines and strokes of different thicknesses may be used in the same drawing when different thicknesses have different meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: continuous thick line for edging/outlining views and cross-sections; continuous thin line for reference lines, hatching; thin freehand line for delimiting views; thin broken line for hidden edges; dot-dash thin line for axes; thin line terminating in two thick lines for outlines of cross-sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference lines (leading lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference lines between reference signs and the details referred to may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must originate in immediate proximity of the reference sign and extend to the feature. Reference lines may be omitted for certain signs which then indicate the surface or cross-section on which they are placed; such signs may be underlined to indicate omitted lines. Reference lines must be executed like other lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of arrows in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at the end of reference lines provided their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freestanding arrow indicates entire section towards which it points; arrow touching a line indicates the surface shown by the line looking along direction; arrows may show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of cross-sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific conditions govern how cross-sections are indicated, identified and represented (Rule 11.13(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a figure is a cross-section on another figure, the latter should indicate the position of the section and may indicate viewing direction by arrows. Each end of the cross-section line should be marked with the same Arabic or Roman numeral identifying the figure. Cross-sections represent the part behind the cutting surface; cutting surfaces must be precisely defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatching in cross-sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-sections must be hatched with regularly spaced parallel oblique strokes; spacing chosen based on total area to be hatched (Rule 11.13(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must not impede reading of reference signs; hatching may be broken where signs are inserted. Certain hatching types may have conventional meanings. Hatching should be at a substantial angle (preferably 45°). Parts of same item hatched same manner; juxtaposed different elements angled differently. For large areas, hatching can be confined to an edging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale should be such that all essential details can be clearly distinguished when reduced to two-thirds (Rule 11.13(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional cases the scale may be graphically represented. Indications like 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted as they lose meaning upon reproduction in different formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion within figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each element of each figure must be in proportion to other elements except where different proportion is indispensable for clarity (Rule 11.13(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred alternative to differing proportions within a figure is adding a supplementary figure showing the enlarged element. Where an enlarged element is shown separately, indicate its location in the initial figure by a finely drawn circle or dot-dash circle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of numbers, letters and reference signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers, letters and reference signs on drawings must be simple and clear and not used with brackets, inverted commas, circles or outlines (Rule 11.13(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signs for minutes/seconds/degrees are permitted. Text should be laid out in same direction as the diagram to avoid rotating the sheet. Avoid placing signs in closed/complex parts that interfere with comprehension; place signs as close as possible to the part indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum size for numbers and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: A minimum size of 0.32 cm is required for all numbers and letters used on the drawings so reduction to two-thirds remains legible (Rule 11.13(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latin alphabet should normally be used; Greek alphabet accepted where customarily used (e.g., angles, wavelengths).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of reference signs across application
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference signs must be used consistently between description, claims and drawings (Rule 11.13(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference signs not mentioned in the description must not appear in the drawings and vice versa. If pages/paragraphs are deleted, remove corresponding reference signs. If a figure is deleted, delete related reference signs in description and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for reference numbering across variants
rubrics_metrics.description: When several variants or embodiments are described, common features may be identified by prefixed numbers indicating figure and feature (Rule 11.13(m)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., common feature '15' indicated as '115' in Fig.1 and '215' in Fig.2. If used, explain this system in the description to aid readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text matter in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must not contain text matter except a single word or words when absolutely indispensable (Rule 11.11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'water', 'steam', 'open', 'closed', 'section on AB'; for electrical/flow diagrams a few short catch words may be indispensable. Avoid significant amounts of text as it complicates understanding and translation; words must be placed so they can be pasted over if translated without interfering with lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symbols in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Known devices may be illustrated by universally recognized conventional symbols; other signs/symbols may be used if not easily confused (Rule 10.1(d), 10.1(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols must be readily identifiable, simple, and clearly explained in the description. Different hatching types may have conventional meanings regarding material nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of shading
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is permitted provided it assists understanding and does not impede legibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shading may indicate shape of spherical/cylindrical/conical elements or flat parts in perspective. Not permitted for cross-sections. Only spaced lines may be used for shading (no fully blacked areas); lines must be thin, few and contrasting with rest of drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and color drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT makes no provision for photographs or color drawings but they may be submitted where necessary to present what cannot be shown in black and white drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted, they must be on A4 and respect minimum margins. For international publication images will be converted to black and white (not greyscale), which may cause loss of detail. Filing software may indicate presence of photographs/color drawings to trigger a notice that originals are available on PATENTSCOPE. National phase Offices may still require true black and white drawings that do not add subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of reference signs in the description
rubrics_metrics.description: For complex subjects with many drawings, a separate sheet listing all reference signs may be included at the end of the description (Rule 11.13(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list may take any appropriate form and contain reference signs with the designation of the features they denote to facilitate understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious mistakes in drawings may be rectified following Rule 91 procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure in paragraphs 11.033–11.044. Omission of an entire sheet of drawings cannot be rectified without affecting the international filing date (see paragraphs 6.025(i)(b) and 6.026). Changes other than rectification of obvious mistakes are considered amendments (see paragraph 5.162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of drawings during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings can be amended during the international phase only if a demand for international preliminary examination is filed (Article 28, Article 34(2)(b), Article 41(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings may also be amended during the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract serves as a scanning tool for searching in the particular art and assists researchers in deciding whether to consult the full international application (Article 3(3), Rule 8.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It serves only as technical information and cannot be used to interpret the scope of protection sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content: general
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should summarise the disclosure as contained in the description, claims and any drawings and indicate the technical field (Rule 8.1(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft to allow a clear understanding of the technical problem, the gist of the solution, and principal uses. Where applicable include the chemical formula that best characterizes the invention. Abstract should be primarily related to what is new in the art. See WIPO Standard ST.12/A for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content for modifications and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: If invention is a modification, abstract should be directed to the technical disclosure of the modification; if entire disclosure is new abstract should cover entire disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application contains significant disclosure of method of preparation or use, include it. If disclosure involves alternatives, deal with the preferred alternative and identify others succintly; if not possible, mention existence and whether they differ substantially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific items abstract should contain
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable the abstract should include: (1) organization and operation for machines/systems; (2) method of making for articles; (3) identity and preparation for chemical compounds; (4) ingredients for mixtures; (5) steps for processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extensive mechanical and design details of apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract for chemical inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical compounds/compositions, the abstract should give the general nature and use and exemplify a class by a typical example; for processes state type of reaction, reagents and process conditions illustrated by a single example (Rule 8.1(a)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the chemical formula that best characterizes the invention among those contained in the application where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract must not contain statements of merits or speculative applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must not contain statements on the alleged merits or value of the claimed invention or on its speculative application (Rule 8.1(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep abstract factual and technical, avoid promotional or speculative language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be as concise as the disclosure permits; if drafted in English preferably 50–150 words (Rule 8.1(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implied phrases such as 'This disclosure concerns...' or 'This invention relates to...'. Translation guidance gives language-specific ranges likely to translate into 50–150 English words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure to accompany abstract: suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains drawings, the applicant should indicate in the request checklist the number of the drawing figure suggested to be published with the abstract (Rule 3.3(a)(iii), Rule 8.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate one figure number in the checklist for front-page publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which figure should accompany the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The figure illustrating the abstract must be the one which best characterizes the claimed invention and must be chosen from the drawings; generally only one figure should be indicated (paragraph 5.171).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid figures with significant amounts of text. Exceptionally more than one figure may be used if necessary. If no figure is useful, indicate none. A figure accompanying the abstract may not be included within the abstract text itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference signs in the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains drawings, each main technical feature mentioned in the abstract and illustrated by a drawing should be followed by a reference sign in parentheses (Rule 8.1(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference numerals used in the abstract must correspond to those indicated in the relevant figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of abstract sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be presented on a separate sheet which must appear after the claims and be numbered accordingly (Section 207, Rule 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract sheet must comply with the same physical requirements as the description (refer to paragraph 5.105).

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing or defective abstract procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office finds the abstract missing it invites the applicant to furnish it within two months; application can be considered withdrawn if not furnished (Article 14(1)(a)(iv), Article 14(1)(b), Rule 26.2, Rule 38.2, Rule 38.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If RO does not invite the applicant, the International Searching Authority (ISA) establishes an abstract. Applicant may submit comments to the abstract established by the ISA within one month from mailing of the international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of abstract after ISA establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may submit proposed modifications of the abstract to the ISA until one month from the date of mailing of the international search report (Rule 38.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA decides whether to modify the abstract accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of immoral, disparaging or irrelevant matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application may not contain matter contrary to morality or public order, disparaging statements or obviously irrelevant or unnecessary matter (Article 21(6), Rule 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office, ISA, Authority for supplementary search or International Bureau may suggest corrections when lack of compliance with Rule 9 is noted (see paragraph 6.052 for correction procedure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical terminology and signs requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain requirements exist as to technical terminology and signs to be used (metric system, etc.) as specified in Rule 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed technical terminology to ensure acceptance by all designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: General physical requirements for the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must comply with physical requirements such as fitness for reproduction, paper to be used, manner of writing (generally typewritten or printed) (Article 3(4)(ii), Article 14(1)(a)(v), Rule 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details are in Rule 11 and are similar to requirements applied by major national Patent Offices and regional Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Latin characters in names/addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Names or addresses written in characters other than Latin must be transliterated or translated into English (Rule 4.16).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 4.16 for transliteration/translation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies required
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application and any required translation must be filed in one, two or three copies depending on the receiving Office (Rule 11.1(a), Rule 11.1(b), Rule 21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ultimately there must be three copies: home copy (receiving Office), record copy (International Bureau), and search copy (International Searching Authority) (Article 12, Rule 21.1, Rule 22.1(a), Rule 23.1(a), Section 305). If fewer copies filed, receiving Office prepares additional copies and may charge a fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: When translation must be furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed in a language accepted by the receiving Office but not accepted by the ISA conducting the search, the applicant must furnish a translation (Rule 12, Rule 12.3, Rule 21.1, Rule 22.1(a), Rule 23.1(a), Section 305bis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the receiving Office receives the translation it forwards copies as 'record copy - translation', 'home copy - translation' and 'search copy - translation' to the relevant Offices. If translation filed in fewer copies than required, RO prepares additional copies and may charge a fee.
